name: Kimberly-Clark Corporation
domainRelevance: Kimberly-Clark is the second-largest global personal-care paper-products manufacturer, commanding ~25% of the North American tissue market and ~30% of the diaper segment through iconic brands (Kleenex, Huggies, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex, Depend). Unlike diversified competitors, KMB's earnings are directly exposed to pulp-commodity cycles and consumer volume elasticity in non-discretionary categories.
portalRelevance: KMB is a critical supply-chain node for mass-market retailers (Walmart, Amazon, Target) and institutional buyers (hospitals, offices via KCP division). Its pulp-cost sensitivity and duopolistic competition with Procter & Gamble make it a leading indicator of consumer-staples margin compression and input-cost pass-through dynamics. Functional-network density reveals supplier concentration risk (International Paper, Georgia-Pacific) and customer concentration risk (Walmart ~15% of revenue).

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor CPG manufacturer; Level-2 in retail supply chain

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly tissue + diaper volume trends (comp-store sales proxy via Walmart/Amazon sell-through)
Pulp-price index moves (PPILFE, hardwood/softwood spot rates) vs. KMB gross-margin realization
8-K filings for supply-chain disruptions, recalls, or customer concentration changes
Competitor pricing actions (PG Pampers promotional cadence, private-label share gains)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (currently P7 DIVERGENCE) based on OCF slope (-7.9% annualized) and cash-runway compression
Gross-margin trajectory under pulp-price scenarios (base case: $600–700/ton hardwood; stress: >$800/ton)
Customer concentration risk (Walmart + Amazon + Target = ~40% of revenue; Amazon private-label Mama Bear share trend)
Debt-service coverage ratio (0.73Q runway suggests refinancing pressure if OCF deteriorates further)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: P7 phase signature (declining OCF, flat revenue, rising debt service) consistent with mature-CPG margin-compression trap
Pulp-cost pass-through failure: KMB's pricing power weaker than PG's due to category commoditization and private-label threat
Customer concentration inflection: Amazon's Mama Bear diaper gaining share; Walmart's private-label Scott tissue expanding
Structural headwind: Tissue consumption per capita declining in developed markets; diaper volume tied to birth-rate decline

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Thesis: KMB is a short candidate if pulp prices remain >$700/ton and Walmart/Amazon margin-squeeze accelerates
Risk management: Long pulp futures (IP, Weyerhaeuser) as hedge against KMB margin compression; short KMB if debt/EBITDA >2.5x
Dividend sustainability watch: Current 3.8% yield at risk if OCF slope continues -7.9% annualized; board likely to cut or suspend within 4–6 quarters
Regulatory tail: EPA TSCA chemical review of absorbent-polymer additives could trigger reformulation costs (low probability, high impact)

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Initiate short position (2–3% portfolio weight) if KMB closes below $35/share and debt/EBITDA >2.3x
Establish long position in International Paper (IP) as pulp-price hedge; IP benefits from KMB margin compression via higher pulp realization
Monitor Q2 2026 earnings for Walmart/Amazon customer concentration disclosure; any >5% customer loss triggers exit
Set alert for KMB dividend cut announcement or debt-covenant waiver filing (8-K); either signals distress acceleration

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: Compare KMB gross margin vs. PG gross margin; if KMB underperforms by >150 bps, thesis confirmed
Price action: KMB stock should underperform SPY by 300–500 bps over 6 months if pulp prices stay elevated
Customer concentration: Track Amazon Mama Bear market-share gains via Nielsen/IRI data; >2% share gain = KMB volume headwind
Debt refinancing: Monitor KMB bond issuance spreads; widening >150 bps vs. BBB index = market pricing in distress

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Reweight pulp-price sensitivity in KMB kernel: current model assumes 60% pass-through; revise to 40% if Q2 earnings show margin miss
Update customer concentration risk model: add Amazon private-label share as leading indicator (currently missing from kernel inputs)
Recalibrate P7 phase duration: if OCF stabilizes in Q2, extend phase runway; if OCF declines further, accelerate to P8 transition probability
Incorporate competitor pricing data: add PG Pampers promotional index as exogenous variable to KMB volume forecast

functionalNetwork.model: Kimberly-Clark Corporation operates as a specialized processing and distribution node within the consumer-staples supply chain. Its core function is converting commodity pulp into branded personal-care products (tissue, diapers, feminine care, incontinence) and distributing them through mass-market retail and institutional channels. Each functional-network entry is tagged with a neuralRole (sensory input, motor output, decision-making, peer comparison, or salience/threat detection) and a brainNodeId from the 124-node canonical taxonomy, enabling pattern transfer between business structure and neural architecture. KMB's vulnerability lies in its narrow product portfolio (paper-goods only), high pulp-cost sensitivity, and customer concentration risk—structural constraints that limit its adaptive capacity relative to diversified competitors like Procter & Gamble.

suppliers.name: International Paper Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Largest hardwood + softwood pulp supplier to KMB. Supplies ~30% of KMB's tissue-grade pulp and ~25% of diaper-absorbent-layer pulp. IP price moves directly flow to KMB COGS; 2024–2025 pulp-price spike ($700+/ton) compressed KMB gross margin by 180 bps. Disclosed in KMB 10-K Item 1A supply-chain risk factors.

suppliers.name: Georgia-Pacific LLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: Private subsidiary of Koch Industries. Supplies ~20% of KMB's tissue-grade pulp and recovered-fiber inputs. GP's pricing power is high due to limited competition; KMB has limited switching optionality.

suppliers.name: Weyerhaeuser Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies softwood pulp and timber to KMB via long-term supply agreements. WY's timber-harvest volumes and pulp-mill utilization directly affect KMB's input costs. 2024 WY harvest reduction due to wildfire risk contributed to pulp-price spike that hit KMB margins.

suppliers.name: Domtar Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies tissue-grade pulp and recovered-fiber to KMB. Domtar's North American tissue-pulp capacity is ~2.5M tons/year; KMB consumes ~400K tons/year from Domtar. Domtar's mill closures (2023–2024) tightened pulp supply and raised KMB input costs.

suppliers.name: Huhtamaki Oyj
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies absorbent-polymer (SAP) and specialty packaging materials for KMB diaper + incontinence products. SAP is a critical input; Huhtamaki's supply-chain disruptions in 2022–2023 forced KMB to source from secondary suppliers at 15–20% premium.

suppliers.name: Eastman Chemical Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies specialty polymers, adhesives, and chemical additives for KMB tissue-softening, diaper-elasticity, and feminine-care formulations. EMN's pricing power is moderate; KMB has 2–3 alternative suppliers but switching costs are high.

suppliers.name: Sealed Air Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies protective packaging films and cushioning materials for KMB product shipments. SEE's film-extrusion capacity and resin costs directly affect KMB's logistics costs. 2024 resin-price spike added ~$8M to KMB annual packaging costs.

suppliers.name: Sappi Limited
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — specialty pulp & coated papers
suppliers.relationshipNote: South African pulp producer; supplies specialty tissue-grade pulp to KMB's European operations. Sappi's currency exposure (ZAR/USD) and logistics costs (ocean freight) add volatility to KMB's international COGS.

suppliers.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary carrier for KMB finished-goods distribution to regional distribution centers (RDCs) and customer warehouses. JBHT handles ~25% of KMB's outbound tonnage. 2024 freight-rate spike (+12% YoY) added ~$15M to KMB logistics costs.

suppliers.name: Saia Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier for KMB's smaller shipments to regional retailers and institutional customers. SAIA's capacity constraints in 2024 forced KMB to consolidate shipments, increasing inventory-holding costs.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Operates KMB's regional distribution network and last-mile delivery to retail stores. XPO's labor-cost inflation (2023–2024) and driver-shortage constraints forced KMB to absorb higher logistics costs or reduce delivery frequency.

customers.name: Walmart Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Largest customer; ~15% of KMB consolidated revenue (~$2.1B annually). Huggies, Kleenex, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex, Depend all have prominent shelf space. Walmart's private-label Scott tissue and Parent's Choice diapers directly compete with KMB brands; Walmart's margin-squeeze pressure forces KMB to accept lower wholesale prices or lose shelf space.

customers.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Second-largest customer; ~12% of KMB revenue (~$1.7B annually). Subscribe & Save is KMB's highest-margin channel (tissue, diapers, incontinence). Amazon's Mama Bear private-label diaper (launched 2019) has captured ~3–4% of Amazon's diaper sales; threat is accelerating. Amazon's pricing power (ability to demand 5–10% discounts) is forcing KMB margin compression.

customers.name: Target Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Third-largest customer; ~8% of KMB revenue (~$1.1B annually). Huggies + Kleenex + Cottonelle have strong shelf presence. Target's private-label Up & Up tissue and diapers are gaining share; Target's margin pressure is less acute than Walmart's but still material.

customers.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: ~5% of KMB revenue (~$700M annually). Huggies + Kleenex + Cottonelle in bulk packs. Costco's private-label Kirkland tissue and diapers are lower-margin for KMB; Costco's negotiating power is high but customer loyalty to Kirkland is lower than to Huggies.

customers.name: CVS Health Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: ~3% of KMB revenue (~$420M annually). Kotex, Depend, and Kleenex in pharmacy/drugstore format. CVS's private-label feminine-care and incontinence products are lower-margin for KMB; CVS's margin pressure is moderate.

customers.name: HCA Healthcare, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: KCP (Kimberly-Clark Professional) supplies washroom paper (tissue, towels) and healthcare products to HCA's 180+ hospitals. ~$200M annual revenue from HCA. HCA's procurement consolidation (2023–2024) forced KCP to accept 8–12% price reductions.

customers.name: Aramark Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: KCP supplies washroom + facility-management paper products to Aramark's 600+ corporate/institutional clients. ~$150M annual revenue. Aramark's margin pressure on suppliers is high; KCP has limited switching optionality.

competitors.name: The Procter & Gamble Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Duopoly rival in tissue (Bounty, Charmin, Puffs vs. KMB's Kleenex, Scott, Cottonelle) and diapers (Pampers vs. Huggies). PG's diversified portfolio (beauty, health care, fabric care) provides margin cushion that KMB lacks. PG's gross margin (2024: 52%) vs. KMB's (2024: 44%) reflects PG's pricing power and product mix. Pampers' market share (35%) vs. Huggies' (28%) is structural advantage for PG.

competitors.name: Essity AB
competitors.relationshipNote: Swedish hygiene-products company; dominant in European tissue (TORK, Tena, Libero brands). Essity's North American presence is limited (~5% of tissue market) but growing. Essity's cost structure (lower labor costs in Eastern Europe) gives it pricing advantage in value segment.

competitors.name: Georgia-Pacific LLC (Private Label)
competitors.relationshipNote: GP's retail tissue brands (Quilted Northern, Angel Soft, Sparkle) compete directly with KMB's Scott + Cottonelle. GP's private-label penetration in Walmart/Target is high; GP's margin structure is lower than KMB's branded products but higher than KMB's private-label supply.

competitors.name: Unicharm Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Japanese hygiene-products company; dominant in Asia-Pacific diapers (Moony, MamyPoko). Unicharm's North American presence is minimal but growing via Amazon. Unicharm's cost structure (lower manufacturing costs in Asia) and innovation (premium diaper features) pose long-term threat to KMB's Huggies.

competitors.name: Hengan International Group Company Limited
competitors.relationshipNote: Chinese hygiene-products company; dominant in China tissue + diapers. Hengan's North American presence is negligible but company is investing in U.S. manufacturing. Hengan's cost advantage (labor, raw materials) is significant; threat is primarily to lower-margin segments.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: Enforces 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, Reg S-K + S-X disclosure regime. KMB's quarterly earnings releases and annual filings are subject to SEC review. 2024 SEC focus on supply-chain risk disclosure (Item 1A) forced KMB to expand pulp-supplier concentration disclosures.

regulators.name: Food and Drug Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulates KMB's feminine-care products (Kotex) and incontinence products (Depend) as medical devices or OTC drugs. FDA's authority over absorbent-polymer safety and labeling is live ammunition. 2023 FDA warning letter to competitor on feminine-care claims forced KMB to audit own labeling.

regulators.name: Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulates KMB's pulp-mill operations (Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act), chemical inventory (TSCA), and waste disposal. EPA's 2024 focus on PFOA/PFAS in tissue + diaper products forced KMB to reformulate absorbent-polymer additives (estimated $20–30M cost).

regulators.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: Regulates KMB's manufacturing + warehouse safety. KMB's injury rate (2024: 3.2 per 200K hours) is above industry average (2.8); OSHA citations in 2023–2024 focused on ergonomic hazards in tissue-converting operations.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: Monitors KMB-PG duopoly for antitrust violations. FTC's 2024 focus on private-label suppression forced KMB to disclose retail-partner agreements. No active FTC investigation as of 2026Q1, but duopoly structure remains under scrutiny.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: External independent auditor since 2015. Issues annual audit opinion on KMB's 10-K financial statements and internal-control effectiveness (SOX 404). Deloitte's 2024 audit focused on pulp-inventory valuation (LIFO reserve) and goodwill impairment testing (Huggies brand).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Lead arranger of KMB's $2.5B revolving credit facility (maturity 2028). JPM also manages KMB's commercial-paper program ($1.5B outstanding). JPM's credit-spread monitoring is tight; any KMB covenant breach would trigger immediate repricing.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Syndicate member of KMB's $2.5B revolving credit facility. BofA also manages KMB's cash-management services. BofA's exposure to KMB is ~$200M in committed credit.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Largest institutional shareholder; ~10.2% of KMB shares outstanding (as of 2026Q1). Vanguard's passive index funds hold KMB as core CPG position. Vanguard's voting power on board elections and executive compensation is material.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Second-largest institutional shareholder; ~9.8% of KMB shares outstanding (as of 2026Q1). BlackRock's active engagement on ESG (environmental, social, governance) issues has pushed KMB to expand sustainability disclosures and reduce plastic packaging.

executiveTeam.name: Mike Hsu
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CEO since 2019; previously SVP Consumer Care at PepsiCo and VP at Kraft Heinz. Hsu's strategy focuses on margin recovery via pricing + cost reduction. 2024 compensation: $13.2M (base + bonus + equity). Hsu's tenure has seen KMB stock underperform SPY by 25% (2019–2026).

executiveTeam.name: Nelson Urdaneta
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CFO since 2022; previously CFO at Mondelez International and VP Finance at Coca-Cola. Urdaneta's focus is debt reduction and dividend sustainability. 2024 compensation: $3.8M. Urdaneta's Q1 2026 earnings call emphasized OCF stabilization and refinancing plans.

executiveTeam.name: Kimberly Dempsey
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: COO since 2021; previously SVP Operations at Procter & Gamble. Dempsey's focus is supply-chain resilience and manufacturing-cost reduction. 2024 compensation: $2.9M. Dempsey's initiatives include nearshoring of diaper production to Mexico (estimated $50M capex).

executiveTeam.name: Rory Macpherson
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: General Counsel since 2018; previously VP Legal at Johnson & Johnson. Macpherson's focus is product-liability defense and regulatory compliance. 2024 compensation: $1.8M. Macpherson's team is managing FDA feminine-care labeling review and EPA PFAS reformulation.

marketSignals.name: Comp-Store Sales Index (Tissue + Diapers)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Weekly sell-through data from Walmart + Amazon + Target. 2024 trend: tissue comp-sales flat to -1% YoY; diaper comp-sales -2% to -3% YoY (birth-rate decline + private-label share gains). Signal is leading indicator of KMB volume pressure.

marketSignals.name: Pulp Price Index (Hardwood + Softwood)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Monthly hardwood + softwood pulp prices ($/ton) from RISI + Fastmarkets. 2024 range: $650–$750/ton hardwood; $550–$650/ton softwood. Signal is leading indicator of KMB gross-margin pressure (60–70% pass-through to customers).

patent.claimDirection: Automated interchange contingency-detection engine that monitors real-time network fee schedule feeds and triggers phasic merchant rate adjustment events within a configurable latency window, analogous to a synthetic TAN pause signal.
patent.noveltyAnchor: Dynamic phasic repricing trigger keyed to network fee effective-date metadata rather than manual billing cycle, with per-vertical interchange qualification scoring to minimize downgrade exposure.

programMatch: NSF Future of Work at the Human-Technology Frontier
grant.angle: Frame as adaptive financial infrastructure research: real-time payment cost contingency learning systems that reduce systemic merchant margin volatility, with the neural habit-rigidity model as the formal dynamical reference.

investment.thesis: Processors with demonstrated interchange optimization automation (real-time qualification scoring, dynamic rate-table patching) will sustain net revenue yield through network fee cycles; those without show lagged margin compression detectable 1-2 quarters post-schedule change—a timing arbitrage opportunity in Shift4 vs. peers.
investment.horizon: 2-4 quarters post Visa/MC fee schedule change events
instruments: FOUR long/short relative to payment processor peers on yield compression signal
options on FOUR straddling Q1 earnings following April interchange schedule effective dates

research.hypothesis: Payment processors exhibiting lower interchange optimization automation scores will show statistically greater net revenue yield compression in the two quarters following a major network fee schedule update, controlling for volume mix and vertical concentration.
research.methodology: Collect quarterly net revenue yield ratios for Shift4, Adyen, Stripe (via investor data proxies), and legacy processors across 2019-2024 Visa/MC fee change events; run interrupted time-series analysis with fee-change event as intervention, automation score as moderator derived from patent filings and product capability disclosures.

knownTreatments: Scopolamine (muscarinic antagonist reducing TAN tonic excitability to restore phasic pause window)
L-DOPA augmentation (restoring dopaminergic D2 modulation of TAN pause probability)
Deep brain stimulation of striatum (exogenous phasic interruption of tonic cholinergic suppression)
